Properties Slashed 40-90% Off Market in Midland County, Michigan

If you’re looking for a way to score real estate at incredible discounts in Midland County, Michigan, you’re in the right place. The County Tax Foreclosure Auction offers a rare opportunity to purchase properties at up to 90% off market value. Here’s everything you need to know about how to get started, what to expect, and how you can take advantage of these incredible discounts at the next auction.

What is a Tax Deed Auction?

A Tax Deed Auction in Midland County happens when property owners fail to pay their taxes. The county then sells the property to recover the unpaid taxes and other associated costs. When you buy a tax deed, you’re purchasing the property itself (not just the lien), meaning you gain full ownership after completing the sale.

For example, a property worth $100,000 could be available for just $10,000 to $60,000 during a tax deed sale. That’s a significant discount, making tax deed investing a popular strategy for savvy investors looking for a deal.

Why You Should Invest in Midland County’s Tax Deeds?

  1. Buy Properties at Steep Discounts (40-90% Off Market Value) Midland County’s tax deed sales allow you to acquire real estate at a fraction of its actual market value. Whether you’re an investor looking to flip properties or simply searching for a great deal, this is an opportunity you don’t want to miss.
  2. Potential for Multiple Auctions If a property doesn’t sell at the first auction, the county may hold up to two additional auctions for unsold properties. This increases the chances of snagging a property at a reduced price.
  3. Quick Process with Immediate Payment Unlike other real estate deals that may take months to finalize, Midland County tax deed auctions require you to complete the payment on the same night. This quick turnaround is ideal for investors looking for fast-paced opportunities.
  4. No Redemption Period Unlike tax lien sales, there’s no redemption period for tax deed sales. Once you win the bid and pay, the property is yours, free and clear of unpaid taxes.

How to Participate in Midland County’s Tax Deed Auction

Registration and Bidding Process
The auction in Midland County is in-person only—no online or sealed bids are allowed. To participate, show up at 4:15 PM on the day of the sale to register and receive your bid number. Ensure you have a valid ID as only winning bidders will need to officially register.

  • Minimum Bid Increments:
  • For properties with a bid under $1,000: Increments of $50.
  • For properties over $999: Increments of $100.
  • For properties priced over $10,000: Increments of $500.

Payment Information:
After winning a bid, payment is due the same night. Be sure to bring the necessary funds with you to the auction. Payment methods include cash, certified checks, bank approval letters, and credit cards (with a 2.75% processing fee). Failure to make payment will result in forfeiting your winning bid.

Required Affidavit
Every winning bidder must sign an affidavit confirming that they do not owe any back taxes or fines in Midland County. This is an important step to ensure the integrity of the auction process and avoid any complications during the sale.

Pro Tips for Successful Tax Deed Investing in Midland County

  • Do Your Research: Before bidding, research each property thoroughly. Midland County doesn’t guarantee land usability or access, so it’s essential to investigate any issues, such as zoning laws or environmental restrictions.
  • Prepare Your Funds: Make sure you have enough funds available for immediate payment on auction day, as payments are due on the spot.
  • Affidavit Requirement: Be ready to sign an affidavit confirming you don’t owe any back taxes or fines in Midland County. This is a legal requirement to participate in the auction.
  • Monitor Future Auctions: If a property doesn’t sell, the county might hold two more auctions, giving you another chance to bid.

FAQs About Midland County Tax Auction

1. What happens if a property doesn’t sell at the first auction?
If a property doesn’t sell at the first auction, Midland County may hold up to two additional auctions for unsold properties, often at lower starting prices.

2. Can I bid online for these properties?
No, the auction is in-person only. You must be physically present at the auction to place your bids.

3. What payment methods are accepted?
Accepted payment methods include cash, certified checks, bank approval letters, and credit cards (with a 2.75% processing fee).
